correctness.rationale: Every algebra unit is diagonal plus square-zero radical. Fixed diagonal labels are invariant under conjugacy; nonresonant radical arrows contribute exactly field-size powers, and resonant supports have torus stabilizer size equal to the multiplicative-group size raised to the number of graph components. This establishes every class and its size with no missing or repeated support orbit. The subset expansion, Tutte identity, forest recurrence and cycle transfer-matrix formula follow by exact finite algebra. Independent direct group conjugation agrees in 17 examples over fields of orders 2, 3 and 4. Residual computational limitations: finite tests do not prove the general identity.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary papers cover qualitative torus/unipotent conjugacy in incidence monoids and enumeration in different graphical nilpotent groups. Neither supplies the complete conjugacy-class size polynomial here. Previously published simple additive commutator-fiber calculations for Kronecker algebras do not yield this unit-group class-size distribution without a separate unit-conjugacy analysis. The new assessed contribution is an explicit complete two-variable spectrum with matroid invariance and forest/cycle formulas, not the standard torus decomposition or the classical Tutte polynomial.
residual_risks: An equivalent orbit distribution could be present in literature on finite diagonal tori acting on coordinate modules or graph-invariant point counts.

value.rationale: The conjugacy-class size histogram is a complete, motivated invariant of the finite unit group, finer than the total class number. The bivariate refinement determines each class-size factor, establishes orientation invariance and matroid control, and yields full forest and unicyclic closed formulas at arbitrary field size. These deductions are nontrivial structural enumerations rather than numerical experiments.
